title: a passed audit must survive a clean fleet rebase of an unchanged change (ADR-0105 rungs B1–B4)
summary: Operator directive 2026-09-26: a change that passed audit must not be blocked by a process issue. Today every clean fleet rebase re-runs Build and Audit, because the explanation base binding is invalidated before RUNG 0 (cycles 1698 and 1701, 20–30 minutes plus an LLM round each). Review found RUNG 0 has never fired in worktree mode (F1), a written verdict would not bind at ship (F2), the base SHA sits inside the audited patch (F3), the failed ship's inbox consumption rides in the diverged commit (F4), and RUNG 0 artifacts live in the worktree (F5). Rung 0, the worktree-mode tree binding, ships on fix/ship-trusts-a-passed-audit.
fix: Implement docs/architecture/adr/0105-identity-preserving-fleet-rebase.md rung by rung, test-first, each merged at a wave boundary: B2 RebindIdenticalRebase (per-path byte-identity proof, lineage-aware Verify), then B1 unwind plus reordered recovery, then B3 repaired RUNG 0 with F5, then B4 ship carry acceptance. The test list and mutation map are in docs/research/2026-09-26-identity-preserving-rebase-design-review.md.
acceptance: each mutation in the design review's mutation map is killed by its named test
